title: Indian-Origin Surya Midha, 22, Becomes Youngest Self-Made Billionaire With AI Startup Mercor
excerpt: The Bay Area college dropout built an AI hiring platform now valued at $10 billion, beating Zuckerberg's timeline to the billionaire club.
body:
The Rise: Surya Midha, a 22-year-old Indian-origin entrepreneur, has become the world's youngest self-made billionaire through Mercor, an AI recruitment platform he co-founded with high school friends Adarsh Hiremath and Brendan Foody. The San Francisco-based startup, launched in 2023, hit a staggering $10 billion valuation after closing a $350 million Series C funding round in late 2025, making all three founders billionaires before their 23rd birthdays.

Midha, who left Georgetown University's School of Foreign Service to pursue Mercor full-time, built the company around a deceptively simple insight: as AI labs race to train increasingly powerful models, they need vast armies of human experts to label data, test outputs, and provide feedback. Mercor connects these skilled workers with companies like OpenAI, Google, and Meta, reportedly paying out $1.5 million per day to its talent network.

Why It Matters: The company's revenue trajectory tells the story of AI's insatiable appetite for human intelligence. Mercor surged from $100 million to $500 million in annual revenue during 2025 alone, riding the wave of human-in-the-loop AI training. All three co-founders are Thiel Fellows, recipients of Peter Thiel's program that pays promising young entrepreneurs $100,000 to skip college and build companies.

The achievement carries particular resonance for the Indian-American community. Midha and Hiremath, both of Indian origin, join a growing list that includes Sundar Pichai, Satya Nadella, and Arvind Krishna at the helm of America's biggest tech companies. For the 4.4 million Indian-Americans, many of whom arrived through the same H-1B and student visa pipeline, Midha's story reinforces the community's outsized presence in American tech entrepreneurship.

The Catch: Mercor's meteoric rise has not been without turbulence. In early 2026, the company suffered a supply-chain cyberattack that exposed 4 terabytes of sensitive data, triggering lawsuits and causing some clients to pause contracts. How the young founders navigate this crisis will test whether Mercor's valuation reflects durable value or peak-cycle exuberance.

What to Watch: The AI training data market is projected to exceed $30 billion by 2028. If Mercor can weather its security challenges and maintain its growth clip, Midha could become one of the defining tech founders of his generation.
nri_angle: Midha and co-founder Hiremath are both Indian-origin, adding to Silicon Valley's growing list of Indian-American tech billionaires.
author: Diaspora Desk
